pr_title: Modify ossl_provider_forall_loaded() to avoid locking for the callbacks
pr_body:
This avoids recursive lock issues by taking a copy of the provider list and he callbacks are made without holding the store lock.

Fixes #14251

- [x] documentation is added or updated
- [ ] tests are added or updated

issue_context.title: ossl_provider_forall_loaded should not hold a lock while calling the user callback
issue_context.body:
A user callback could do almost anything, so a deadlock is a very likely outcome.

This is very similar to the issue encountered in #14225 and fixed by #14250
comments: There have been other cases of this exact problem.  Perhaps we should review all of the _for all_ and _do all_ type calls.

> There have been other cases of this exact problem. Perhaps we should review all of the _for all_ and _do all_ type calls.

Please open a new issue.
Issue #14285 deals with checking the rest of the _forall_ loops.

review_comments: Not all elements have had their reference count incremented on the error path.  Pop_free always processes all elements.
Is the cb ever likely to do ossl_provider_free()? What happens in that scenario?

If the callback _owns_ a reference to the provider, it is entitled to free it.  It shouldn't free the reference that this function has --> it doesn't own it.  If the callback frees the provider (and no other references exist), the provider will persist until this function frees it later.

This isn't a case I'm too concerned about, the ref counting is more to avoid threading issues.

It would be possible to more eagerly free the local references to providers, but it doesn't seem all that useful.
I was thinking of the case where the for_all is used to perform a free of its objects..
That works.  They hang around until this function frees them after the callbacks are all done.
Is i correct in the case where it does the goto err_unlock?
Yes, that's why the loop variables get swapped.
